findings.title: Cancelled running tasks become unclaimable after lease recovery
findings.reason: request_cancel sets cancel_requested=true while a running task remains nonterminal. _recover_expired_tx later changes that task to queued without clearing cancel_requested, while claim_next only claims queued rows with cancel_requested=false. The expired attempt is recorded, but the task can never be reclaimed or settled.

findings.title: Missing authenticated public user ID is silently replaced by the internal user ID
findings.reason: Both HTTP task creation and IF2 context construction use session.user_public_id or session.user_id. The service only rejects an empty actor_public_id, so a session missing the required public identifier can be resolved under an internal identifier, producing the wrong identity or accepting a task instead of the frozen required_input_missing/422 before-enqueue failure.

findings.title: Frontend renders a successful result before final receipt settlement
findings.reason: record_execution_result writes result_projection while the task is waiting_web_readback and no receipt exists. The generic task result view applies is-success solely from task.result.ok, so it can display a success result during the pre-settlement window. The separate settlement presentation correctly requires the terminal stage and receipt, but that guard is not applied to the generic result block.

findings.title: Receipt settlement does not revalidate the frozen relationship or project recovery linkage
findings.reason: Enqueue stores account_binding in the invocation, but settlement looks up the current active row only by tenant, actor and owned account, then copies its current relationship id, platform and digest into the receipt without comparing them with the invocation binding. The task foreign key likewise pins only tenant/actor/owned-account, so mutable relationship metadata can drift between enqueue and settlement. The receipt projection omits recoveryOfAttemptId; that recovery field is exposed separately by get_settlement rather than being part of the same receipt projection.

findings.title: Independent-review read scope was exceeded
findings.reason: Two read-only search commands used a broad backend/openclaw_app tree and frontend/src/media glob expansion instead of only the frozen 31 files. No file was written and no network or remote system was accessed, but the allowlist and zero-write review procedure prohibit expanding the read scope; an independent rerun is required before acceptance.
